studies.Title: Low-carbohydrate diet score and risk of bladder cancer: Findings from a prospective cohort study.
studies.Authors: Pham YT, Wang R, Yuan JM, Luu HN
studies.Timing: Baseline dietary assessment with 17.6 years mean follow-up, 1993–2015
studies.Population: Chinese men and women aged 45–74 years in the Singapore Chinese Health Study
studies.Smoking Status: Never versus ever smokers adjusted in the multivariable model
studies.comparison_type: Per-SD increment in animal-based low-carbohydrate diet score

sample_size.excerpt: We identified 250 incident cases of bladder cancer among 61 321 study participants of the SCHS who were free of cancer at baseline after a mean (standard deviation) follow‐up of 17.6 (5.3) years (or 819 573 person‐years).
sample_size.location: Patients and Methods, Ascertainment of bladder cancer cases

cases.excerpt: After 17.6 years of follow-up with 819 573 person-years, 250 participants developed bladder cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: We found a statistically significant, positive association for bladder cancer risk with increasing level of animal-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.02-1.32; P trend = 0.01), but a null association with an increased level of plant-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.91-1.28, P trend = 0.78).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We found a statistically significant, positive association for bladder cancer risk with increasing level of animal-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.02-1.32; P trend = 0.01), but a null association with an increased level of plant-based LCD (HRper-SD increment = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.91-1.28, P trend = 0.78).

design.excerpt: We used data from the Singapore Chinese Health Study, a prospective cohort study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: LCD scores were derived from the semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire at baseline.
